title: OOM frequency triage — multi-tenant slot hoarding
body:
Summary:

We observed a sharp increase in OOM incidents across a subset of A100-backed pools during a multi-tenant stress window (spikes in late-night traffic from a small cohort of customers). Unlike prior fragmentation cases, the pattern looks like allocation latencies climb, then a cascade of large cudaMalloc failures follow as the pool becomes effectively unusable for new requests. This doc captures the triage, the working hypotheses (slot hoarding + deferred-free aging), reproducible diagnostic commands, short-term mitigations, and longer-term fixes to prevent recurrence.

Observed symptoms (high level):
- OOM alerts: increased by ~6x over baseline for pool-a100-prod-3 between 2025-08-05 02:00 and 05:00 UTC.
- Request latencies: p95 token latencies increased from 40ms -> 210ms in same window.
- Allocation error rate: cudaMalloc (fallback) errors rose in telemetry; allocator.free_latency_ms distribution shifted right (median 3ms -> 82ms).
- NVSM logs: no pre-existing memory usage plateau — free memory dropped quickly after a traffic spike, then fragmentation-like failures (small free regions present but large contiguous allocations fail).
- Multi-tenant correlation: the failures co-occurred with sustained bursty sessions from 3 tenants (IDs omitted) performing long context generations and repeated streaming completions.

Why this felt different from previous fragmentation notes:
- We saw allocator internals showing many small live reservations (tiny chunk usage) but the adapter that requests contiguous workspace for KV cache/reservations kept trying large allocations and waited.
- There were long tail frees (deferred free path) due to host-side GC scheduling; deferred_free_queue grew.
- The pool-level reservation quotas were not enforced tightly per-tenant; a tenant holding many small live blocks plus inflight async kernels effectively prevented reuse.

Telemetry & tooling we used:
- GPU-level: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 1 (sampling during spike)
- Process-level: pmap + /proc/<pid>/smaps when we could attach
- Runtime metrics: allocator.alloc_count, allocator.free_count, allocator.free_latency_ms (histograms), kvcache.size_by_key, workspace.reservation_count_by_tenant
- Traces: CUPTI lightweight traces for kernel scheduling to see whether kernel queues were piling up, blocking reclaim threads
- Logs: GPUPoolManager debug (reservation/grant events), Allocator debug (slab allocations, coalescence attempts, failed_calloc events)
- Heap map snapshots: produced by our memmap tool (heapmap --dump) before/after spike to visualize contiguous free segments.

Repro steps (non-blocking repro):
1) Create a stress load that opens 12 simultaneous long-lived generation sessions per tenant, with each session streaming tokens (common pattern in customer traffic).
2) Configure client to request long contexts (32k tokens) intermittently to force kvcache allocations to request big contiguous workspace windows.
3) Enable CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC in the runtime and set allocator debug level to verbose.
4) Run for ~20–30 minutes and monitor allocator.free_latency_ms and deferred_free_queue_length.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Slot hoarding by multi-tenant workloads: tenants holding many small live allocations + inflight kernels prevent timely coalescing/eviction and thus contiguous large allocations fail.
2) Deferred-free bottleneck: our deferred free worker thread is single-threaded with a backpressure threshold; when under high kernel load, frees queue and are processed slowly, increasing effective live set.
3) Reuse window mismatch: allocator keeps some slab classes cold for reuse but small-slab churn prevents larger-slab coalescence.
4) KV-cache allocation pattern: repeated ephemeral growth/shrink of kv-reservation size causes fragmentation due to repeated allocate/free cycles at mixed sizes.
5) CUDA driver behavior: in rare cases, driver-level virtual memory mapping prevents immediate reuse until a cudaDeviceSynchronize or kernel completion; this interacts poorly with async frees.

Experiments run + commands (results below):
- Throttle test: limited concurrent sessions per-tenant to 6 (from 12) — OOMs dropped to baseline. Suggests tenant concurrency matters.
- Forced-synchronous-free: introduced a debug build that flushed deferred_free_queue synchronously after each session end; freed faster and reduced fail rate substantially (not safe for prod but useful diagnostically).
- Reserve-per-tenant: configured per-tenant soft-reserve caps (10% pool) — reduced tail OOMs but some tenants saw degraded throughput.
- Aggressive coalescing: patched allocator to run coalescer more frequently during low kernel-util windows — improved contiguous free chunk sizes but increased CPU overhead.

Representative commands used during triage:
- Heap map snapshot: ./tools/heapmap --pid <runtime_pid> --out /tmp/heapmap-before.svg
- Show deferred queue: curl -s http://localhost:9002/metrics | grep deferred_free_queue_length
- Force synchronous free (debug): echo 1 > /proc/<pid>/debug_force_sync_free
- CUPTI trace capture: ./tools/cupti-capture --duration 120 --filter pid:<pid> --out run.cupti

Experiment results (summary):
- Slot hoarding + deferred-free path accounted for ~75% of cases in the test cluster replicated load.
- Simple per-tenant concurrency cap eliminated the cascade but impacted peak throughput for heavy tenants.
- Synchronous drain of deferred frees eliminated OOMs in the repro, confirming frees were the main gating factor.
- Aggressive coalescing improved contiguous chunk availability by ~40% in heapmap snapshots but raised CPU usage on the host by ~11%.

Short-term mitigations (safe to roll quickly):
- Enforce conservative per-tenant concurrency limits on affected pools (config flag rollout) — emergency mitigation to reduce OOM occurrences.
- Increase deferred_free_worker parallelism: small config change to make it 2–3 workers (cost: small CPU increase).
- Add (non-invasive) telemetry: deferred_free_queue_length, avg_free_latency_ms, slab_coalescence_runs_per_min to alert earlier.

Medium/Long-term proposals (requires design + PR work):
1) Per-tenant soft-reservations with elastic reclaim: allow tenants to exceed soft-reserve briefly but trigger prioritized reclaim (preemptible) on exceed.
2) Opportunistic synchronous reclaim at session boundaries: when a session finishes, schedule an immediate reclaim+coalesce for that tenant's freed slabs to reduce transient fragmentation.
3) Rework deferred-free strategy: make deferred frees prioritized by size/class and allow parallel workers to process large-block frees earlier.
4) Slab compaction job: background compaction that moves small live allocations to consolidate free regions (careful: must respect kernel memory pinning and avoid breaking GPU pointers).
5) Better KV-cache growth strategy: prefer growing kv cache in small increments that map to slab classes to avoid mixed-size fragmentation.
6) Pool-level admission control: when contiguous large chunk availability drops under threshold, apply admission backpressure or fall back to smaller model variants.

Telemetry and alerting changes we will ship:
- New alert: sustained deferred_free_queue_length > 1000 for > 5 minutes and avg_free_latency_ms > 50ms triggers P1 triage.
- Dashboard: contiguous_free_ratio_by_pool (visualize % of free memory in blocks >= 256MB, 64MB, 8MB).
- Correlator: create an automated link between tenant reservation spikes and OOM events for faster RCA.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Driver-level gating: do we have evidence of delayed reuse at the CUDA driver level independent of our allocator? Need a controlled test where we free memory synchronously and probe mapping reuse timing.
- Interaction with kernel scheduling: are long-running kernels preventing the deferred_free workers from running (starvation)? CUPTI traces suggested some pressure, but need deeper scheduler telemetry.
- Cost tradeoffs: how much CPU overhead is acceptable for more aggressive coalescing/compaction? Experiment to quantify cost per percent contiguous improvement.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Short-term rollout: @Aisha to roll per-tenant concurrency caps to pool-a100-prod-3 today (2025-08-19).
- Telemetry: @Diego to add deferred_free metrics and contiguous_free_ratio by 2025-08-26.
- Experimentation: @Lena to implement a limited rollout of increased deferred_free_worker_count (2 workers) in staging and measure CPU/contiguous improvements by 2025-09-02.
- Design: Schedule a design review for slab compaction and per-tenant soft-reservation on 2025-09-08 (team: eng-serving-runtime, infra).

Appendix: quick reference notes from the run logs (snippets)
- Allocator: failed_alloc(size=178MB) -> free_latency_p50=86ms free_latency_p95=312ms deferred_free_queue_length=1143
- GPUPoolManager: reservation_grant(tenant=ten-017, size=24MB) repeated 532 times in 300s
- Kernel backlog: avg_launch_wait_ms increased from 2.1 -> 18.6 during spike

Concluding remark:
This incident looks less like classic slow leaking fragmentation and more like a multi-factor cascade: tenant concurrency + deferred-free backlog + mixed-size allocation churn. We have a set of safe short-term mitigations to reduce immediate risk and several promising medium-term fixes that balance CPU cost vs. contiguous memory improvements. The next focus is to add fine-grained telemetry to prove efficacy of the 2-worker deferred-free change and to prototype opportunistic synchronous reclaim at session boundaries.

If you have immediate ideas or want to pair on reproducing the test load, ping me in #eng-serving-runtime or add notes to JIRA INF-3471.
